A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MERIT framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations, analyses of Swiss NSF, NeurIPS and ICLR review data, and runtime experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of MERIT Uniform in Appendix F, Tables 2–3 and Figure 11.

M1.justification: Appendix F adds MERIT Uniform, an optional extension intended to give lottery participants equal selection probabilities through discrete constraints and mixed-integer optimization. The original MERIT procedure remains, with a small control-flow correction from pass to continue in Algorithm 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic review settings and Swiss NSF, NeurIPS 2024 and ICLR 2025 data, including existing interval-generation scenarios. Appendix F evaluates another method on retained coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 11 adds MERIT Uniform alongside MERIT, Swiss NSF, Deterministic (mean) and Deterministic (model). Tables 2–3 also introduce direct comparisons with the uniform variant; no new external baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: The documented data-generation procedures, sample sizes, interval construction, acceptance-rate experiments and utility metrics are retained. Appendix F adds method comparisons without specifying a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix F examines the effect of imposing uniform lottery probabilities on utility, acceptance composition and runtime. This adds a focused constraint analysis; the existing miscalibration, sparsity, model-misspecification and convergence analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing reporting of 50 samples or trials and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals is retained. Figure 11 includes error bars but introduces no different uncertainty procedure, repetition count or significance test.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and Figure 11 add uniform-variant results. For example, Table 3 reports ICLR Gaussian runtimes of 242.222 seconds for MERIT and 2346.693 seconds for MERIT Uniform. Existing displays retain their results, although new Table 2 reports MERIT's ICLR Subjectivity lower probability as 0.49, inconsistent with 0.50 in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix F introduces a constrained optimization formulation for uniform lotteries and explains its mixed-integer, cutting-plane solution. Existing theorems and proofs remain unchanged. The new uniformity constraint (5) is printed for i in [k], although the stated requirement concerns all n candidates.

C1.justification: Section 8 newly claims that MERIT can implement an ex ante optimal uniform lottery satisfying ex post validity, supported by utility comparisons. The abstract and five introductory contributions retain their original scientific claims.

C2.justification: V3 motivates uniform probabilities as potentially more transparent and acceptable, interprets their utility tradeoff, and attributes slower runtime to integer optimization. Appendix F also suggests possible solver improvements. The earlier limitations and future-work discussion remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F explains implementation by initializing Algorithm 4 with additional integer constraints and discloses that no additional solver-parameter optimization was performed. Existing hardware, Gurobi version, data-processing descriptions and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds a connection to randomized social choice and worst-case distortion, with new references to Brandl et al. (2016) and Anshelevich et al. (2021). The introduction adds Feliciani et al. (2024) on funding lotteries. Existing references and positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The title gains the subtitle Applications to Peer Review and Grant Funding. Local copyedits, added paragraphs in Sections 7–8 and a new Appendix F extend the narrative without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the existing paper.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 2–3 and Figure 11 while retaining the earlier displays. Figure 11 extends the utility comparison with another method, some Figure 3 error-bar colors change, and existing appendix figures shift within the layout.

improvement.justification: V3 adds an experimentally examined uniform-lottery option addressing v1's interpretability concern, with useful evidence about utility and substantial runtime costs. The social-choice discussion also improves context. These are limited gains: the core evidence is unchanged, constraint (5) has an indexing inconsistency, and the claim of nearly identical acceptance probabilities is stronger than Table 2 supports.
